body:
The fact that it fails on the first PR means that the processor at least partially doesn't actually support SSE 4.2, the latter just checks support, if it was just the check this would run fine before that PR, and that check checks for cpu flags so it should return true if the CPU works correctly, i.e. it should crash before *and* after #108561, so the CPU seems to report that it does, indeed, not support SSE 4.2

This would possibly be a case of that this CPU doesn't really support it or that there's something else wrong, can you check using CPU diagnostic tools to check if it has the support properly?
I'm not sure I tested with just the first PR. Can you tell me what beta includes only that one but not the runtime check for me to test? I just reverted both in a custom build.

It's in dev5, just try to revert *one* of the PRs and test

I'd suggest trying cpuid (https://www.cpuid.com/) to check what it reports, if it does report support for SSE 4.2 then this is a bug in the check, otherwise it's an issue in your CPU
v4.5.dev5.official [64b09905c] doesn't crash, I can open the editor and run a project, so it's only after the runtime check was added that it won't open.
Good to know! Then it'd be relevant to see what some CPU feature check tool like cpuid reports
What's your Windows version (build number)?
Windows 10 (build 17763)

> Windows 10 (build 17763)

That's ancient (support ended in 2020/2021), it's possible it doesn't support this flag.

Windows 10 LTSC Version 1809 (OS Build 17763) has an extended support end date of 2029-01-09. It still gets updates regularly.
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/release-health/release-information

The CPU was released in May 2014, I don't consider 11 years ancient. Hopefully Godot doesn't go the UE route of forcing more and more recent upgrades. Personally I'm fine with reverting some commits, I only opened this issue to help others as suggested by Godot core team members.

Please check cpuid to see what it reports, if *it* says the CPU lacks SSE 4.2 support then our check isn't the problem probably, that would give us some reference, but no one said that the CPU was ancient

The question comes down to three different options:
1) The CPU is somehow defective in reporting support for the SSE 4.2 flag
2) The CPU or OS doesn't support the specific way this CPU reports support
3) There's something broken in our check for this flag

In the case of 1 we can't really do anything as your device reports incorrectly or has broken support, in the second case we might need to look into alternative ways to detect SSE 4.2 support, and in the third we need to investigate what's wrong there

As linked the Windows 10 LTSC Version 1809 is younger than the CPU, so if you call 2018-11-13 ancient, then you must be calling the CPU ancient too. I just found it dismissive, I'm only trying to help Godot dev team and others by opening an issue.

I'll trust that link since it seems to be widely used but in general I prefer not to run closed software like that. I'll update later.

Please be constructive and assume good intent, the version was old and it was missed that it was long term support, a version of Windows from that old that isn't LTS is ancient as it ended support years ago, but a CPU from that long ago isn't necessarily

You can also check this https://my.schrodinger.com/support/article/243079 for checking support

But without some further details from your end we can't really help, that's what's needed here, please help us help you and try not to jump to the worst assumptions

It's unlikely that CPU is reporting wrong flags, but `IsProcessorFeaturePresent` docs have the following note: "If the HAL does not support detection of the feature, whether or not the hardware supports the feature, the return value is also zero." so it's likely Windows version related.

We can probably call `__cpuid` directly, it should be more accurate.

Then that's a good baseline for determining what's available for testing, one issue eliminated, good to have this reported ahead of 4.5 so we can cover more hardware properly, and we know `__cpuid` can be relied upon in this case at least

One option might be to check `IsProcessorFeaturePresent` first, and if it fails fall back to `__cpuid` as it has some caveats and could theoretically rely on SSE 4.2 internally based on the comments in the PR
Please check if this PR is working for you - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109169
I have used every version since Godot 3.0, and I have never seen this error before. (Godot_v4.5-beta1 to Godot_v4.5-beta3 all worked fine). Why is Godot_v4.5-beta4 behaving unexpectedly?
Check the PR mentioned in the post above, that may resolve the issue with bad CPU detection

that CPU supports SSE 4.2

@Zireael07 Please see the conversation, this is because of a broken check

Windows Server 2019 probably also has a broken flag check like older Windows 10 versions do
